bhi.title: Sharing Jesus with a Hebrew Israelite
bhi.intro: Not to win a street exchange — those are built to be unwinnable. To reach one person whose grievance is real and whose remedy is not.
bhi.html:
Say this before anything else
You, first

"The American church was mostly silent about slavery, and in many places it was worse than silent. That was our failure. I am not going to explain it away."

Say that out loud before you say anything else. Do not soften it. Do not follow it with a defence of the church.

Pulpits defended slavery from the text. Preachers owned people. Whole denominations split rather than call it sin. The silence went on long after the auction blocks closed.

The person in front of you has been told that Christians deny this. Most of the Christians they have met did deny it. When you do not, you become something they have no box for.

This is not a tactic and it is not a warm-up. It is true. It has to be said before you have earned a single other sentence.

Say it in your own words rather than as a formula. If you do not know the history, go and read it before you speak.

The next move will often be that this proves Christianity is a slave master religion. Answer that slowly. The answer is not that the church was fine.

It is that the same book was read in secret in the quarters, by people the preachers were trying to keep quiet, and it is what they sang.

The invitation to work toward
You, off camera

"Would you read Deuteronomy 28 and 30 with me, start to finish, and then Galatians? Just us. No podium and no camera."

Everything on this site is built for that conversation. None of it is built for the street.

The camps teach precept upon precept. That means chains of single lines pulled from all over the Bible. The method is also the weak spot.

Read Deuteronomy 28 from verse 1. Read Isaiah 28 down to verse 13. The chain comes apart on its own. You are not arguing against their verses. You are reading around them.

That is why whole chapters matter more than clever answers. A chapter read together does the work, and nobody has to lose.

Ask for a chapter, not a debate. A chapter has a beginning and an end, and both of you can see them coming.

If they want to trade single verses instead, treat that as a signal. It usually means the exchange is a performance rather than a conversation.

What actually reaches someone in the camps
1

Concede the true half out loud

Cheap grace is a real distortion. The silence on slavery is a real failure. Replacement theology is a real error, and Romans 11:1 forbids it by name. God has not cast off his people. Grant all three before you contest anything.

2

Read whole chapters, never single lines

Ask them to read the chapter aloud. Let the text do the work while you stay quiet. You never have to attack the method, because the method breaks itself.

3

One question, then real silence

Ask who verse 1 is addressed to. Ask what the atonement is when you break the law. These are not gotchas. Each is a real question with no prepared camp answer.

4

Be the Christian still here next month

Street teaching is a stage. Friendship is not. Almost nobody leaves this movement because of an argument. Almost everyone who leaves had one patient person nearby.

The method

Know the strands apart

The 1896 church, the Dimona community, IUIC and ISUPK are not one thing. They disagree, and they do not like each other. The Church of God and Saints of Christ was founded in 1896 by William Saunders Crowdy, a formerly enslaved Union Army veteran. It is still a working denomination.

Move it off the street

A podium, an amplifier, officers and a ring of phones make a stage. Every exchange there is scored by the crowd. Ask for coffee instead. If the answer is no, the exchange was never about the question.

Stay on the one dividing line

The real question is not skin. It is whether a person is put right with God by bloodline and law keeping, or by trusting the Messiah. Keep returning there, gently, however far the talk wanders.

Not the skin colour fight

Jesus was a first-century Judean. He did not look like a European painting. That much is simply true. Defending the painting turns you into the caricature they preach about. Concede it and go to whether he is the Messiah.

Not the hate group label

As a blanket claim it is false. It sweeps in a 130-year-old denomination and a quiet farming village in Israel. It also ends the conversation on the spot. Name a specific teaching if you must name something. Never the whole movement.

Never confuse Dimona with a street camp

Ben Ammi Ben-Israel led a group from Chicago to Liberia in 1967, then to Dimona in Israel in 1969. What grew there is a settled village with schools, farms and its own vegan food industry. The people are peaceable. Lumping them in with a megaphone on a corner tells your friend you learned the movement from a video.

Not the viral clip

Confrontation footage ages badly and gets re-cut. All it tells your listener is which outlet you watch. You trade a durable argument from the text for a throwaway one from the news cycle.

When it turns into theatre
You, calmly

"I am not doing this in front of a camera. I will read the chapter with you any day this week, just the two of us."

Say it once, mean it, and leave the offer open.

A crowd changes what a person can afford to admit. Nobody concedes a point while five men in tunics and a dozen phones are watching. Taking the audience away is not a trick. It is the only condition under which either of you can think.

If the offer is refused, you have still learned something. You have also lost nothing worth keeping.

And if they mock you for leaving, let them. The exchange you walked away from was never the one that changes anybody.

The same rule applies to the phone in your own pocket. Filming your reply for an audience puts you back on the stage you just asked them to leave.

The part that takes years
You, later

"You do not have to agree with me for us to be friends. I am not keeping score, and I am not going anywhere."

People do not walk out of a camp in an afternoon. Leaving costs them a teacher, a schedule, a set of brothers and a story about who they are.

Almost everyone who does leave describes the same thing. One Christian stayed steady, kept turning up, and never treated them as a project.

So plan for a long time. Answer the text when it comes up. Otherwise be a friend, and let the questions arrive on their own schedule.

The camps also make hard predictions. One taught that the year 2000 would bring the reckoning, and it did not come.

Do not crow about that. File it and wait until they raise it themselves, which they eventually will.

When a person starts asking quietly, the last thing they need is an audience or a told-you-so. Give them a kitchen table and an hour.

Expect the questions to come in the wrong order and at the wrong time. Answer the one you are asked rather than the one you prepared.

Learn the history of the movement well enough to be useful. It runs from a church founded in 1896, through a Harlem congregation in 1919, to the camps on the corner today.

Knowing that story is not ammunition. It is how you show a person that you took their world seriously enough to study it.

How it actually goes

People do not join because the chart is convincing. They join because someone finally told them their history was in the Bible.

— the thing to answer, and the thing never to mock

The five questions that do the most work

  1. "Who is Deuteronomy 28:1 addressed to?" Ask them to read it out loud. The chapter names its own audience in the very first line. The whole structure depends on quoting the chapter from the middle. This is the gentlest question here and the one that unsettles most.
  2. "What does Deuteronomy 30 say happens after the curses?" The same covenant that pronounces the curses also promises the gathering back. Read it together rather than summarising it. The curses were never meant to be a permanent identity, and the chapter says so in its own words.
  3. "If salvation is by keeping the law, what is the atonement when you fail?" There has been no altar since AD 70. The system has no answer inside itself. This is the question that reaches people, so ask it once and then stop talking. The silence afterwards is doing more than anything you could add.
  4. "If a white man repents and believes, is he saved?" Ask it gently, with no trap in your voice. The answer shifts from camp to camp. The disagreement inside the movement makes the point far better than you can, and it makes it without you.
  5. "Which teacher do you follow, and where did he learn this?" The movement is young and it splits often. A recovered ancient identity that cannot agree with itself about what it is raises the question quietly. Ask because you want the answer, not because you want the point.

Start here

The identity path walks the one chapter that everything else rests on. Every case page ends with a suggested question and a scripted back-and-forth, so you meet the counter-moves before they meet you.
